newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish political unease puts sell-offs on hold.
newsitem.headline: Turkish political unease puts sell-offs on hold.

text.p: Political turmoil over the past two months has put the government's vital privatisation plans on hold, according to the Privatisation Administration (OIB).

The Islamist-led government has been concentrating solely on warding off an assault by the secularist military since February 28, when a board of top generals and government figures ordered a crack-down on Islamist zeal.
The political unease, as Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan stalled and the military piled on the pressure, has hurt the markets and hindered the workings of government bodies.
The Higher Board of Privatisation, which takes final decisions on sell-offs, has not met since March 29, OIB officials said.

The OIB which set its 1997 privatisation target $4.5 billion says it has only received $23 million from a flurry of sell-offs at the start of the year -- worth $553 million -- because the relevant contracts have not yet been signed.

The sale of facilities owned by the state tourism network Turban has been awaiting the go-ahead from prime minister Necmettin Erbakan since April 14 and the final decisions on bids submitted for seven state-run ports are still awaiting signatures from members of the Higher Board of Privatisation.

And the privatisation of the big state flat steel producer, Eregli Demir Celik, has shown no progress since two bids were received three months ago. The OIB has denied rumours that the sale will be cancelled because the bids are too low.

Turkey's sluggish, 10-year-old privatisation programme got a boost in January when the Constitutional Court finally approved the law governing the sale of the state telecoms company, Turk Telekom, after overturning it twice previously.
Analysts say the partial sale of Turk Telekom shares is unlikely this year.
Turkey has raised around $3 billion through sell-offs since the programme was launched in 1986.
